transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-04-28
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Maya (Crestline CTO), Ravi (Platform Eng), Elena (Product)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on integration paths for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Crestline wants to embed product descriptions, search reranking, and a customer support assistant into their storefront. Primary concerns: latency SLAs for customer-facing flows, cost per token, SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, proxy/gateway setup for egress/rate-limiting, and observability/tracing hooks for our telemetry.

Topics:
- SDKs and examples (LangChain/LlamaIndex)
- Gateway/proxy & VPC/private deployment options
- Rate limits, quotas, burst capacity
- Observability (tracing, per-route metrics, webhooks)
- Security (SAML/SSO, audit logs, KMS)

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick intros?
[00:06] Maya: Hi I'm Maya, CTO at Crestline. We're building a headless commerce platform with heavy product search and personalization.
[00:12] Ravi: Ravi, platform eng, I own infra and secrets.
[00:15] Elena: Elena, PM for search and support flows.
[00:18] Samir: Great, Jules our SE will cover the integration details. Jules?
[00:22] Jules: Thanks Samir. Quick agenda — we want to understand your integration surface: SDKs, connectors like LangChain or LlamaIndex, how you'd route through a gateway or proxy, and what observability hooks you get. Also we'll cover hosted vs dedicated vs private options.
[00:35] Maya: Yep, main ask — we need customer-facing latency under 300ms p95 for simple completions (search re-rank), and sub-second for chat sessions. Cost needs to be predictable; we may start on hosted but likely want dedicated in prod.
[00:50] Ravi: On security — must support SSO (SAML), audit logs, and we prefer keys in our KMS. If dedicated, we need VPC peering.
[01:02] Jules: All familiar. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value: REST/SDK, streaming, and per-route quotas. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and VPC options. Private (on-prem) is available for air-gapped if needed.
[01:18] Maya: For integration, do you have LangChain and LlamaIndex examples? Our ML infra team uses LangChain wrappers heavily.
[01:25] Jules: Yes — we have sample LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors in our SDK repo. I can share a LangChain agent example that uses Redwood's streaming responses for token-by-token UI updates. There might be minor naming mismatches in older samples — some references to 'Redwood Serve' in docs but it's the same API surface.
[01:40] Ravi: How does auth work when we're behind our API gateway? We want to avoid embedding keys in the browser.
[01:45] Samir: Typical pattern is to terminate requests at your backend — your service calls Redwood with an internal API key. We also support proxy gateway modes and can accept requests from a customer-managed proxy.
[01:55] Maya: Can we push through our Istio gateway and apply rate limits there, or do you recommend Redwood rate limiting?
[02:02] Jules: Both. You can do edge rate limiting at Istio (recommended for burst protection) and configure per-route quotas in Redwood for second-layer controls. Redwood's rate limiting integrates with customer token buckets and you can set soft vs hard limits.
[02:18] Ravi: What's the typical failure mode? If we hit dedicated capacity limits, do you fallback to hosted?
[02:24] Jules: We support smart routing/fallback policies: you can route to a lower-cost replica or the hosted pool if dedicated is saturated. That behavior is configurable per route.
[02:34] Elena: Observability — we need traces correlated with our request IDs. Does Redwood support passing trace IDs and returning headers?
[02:41] Jules: Yes — you can send x-request-id or traceparent headers. We surface per-request traces and per-route token cost in the Console. There's also an event webhook for mispredictions or latency spikes.
[02:54] Maya: Do you have sampling controls? We don't want every single call in detail.
[02:58] Jules: You can set sampling rates for traces and we also provide aggregated dashboards with token-level cost and latency histograms.
[03:05] Ravi: From an SDK perspective, our stack is Node backend + Next.js for frontend. We use server-side proxies for sensitive calls. Any gotchas?
[03:12] Jules: Node and Python SDKs are first-class. For Next.js, avoid client-side keys — use your server to proxy. We provide streaming SDK helpers for Node that play nicely with server-sent events.
[03:23] Maya: About LangChain — our prompts live in LlamaIndex with a retrieval layer. How well does Redwood handle big context windows and KV cache?
[03:33] Jules: Our runtime has KV cache management and continuous batching. For retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), we recommend using embeddings + the embeddings endpoint and then the text generation endpoint with pinned context. For very large windows, quantized model variants are available on dedicated nodes.
[03:48] Ravi: Embeddings cost model — do you meter per vector? We need to map to budget forecasts.
[03:53] Samir: Yes, embeddings are billed per-unit (per-embedding call / vector). We'll send the embedding pricing sheet; you can plug in your estimated query/insert volumes.
[04:03] Elena: For POCs, we want to validate latency with a synthetic workload — can Redwood run a benchmark on our behalf?
[04:09] Jules: We can provide a benchmark plan and sample load generator. For dedicated pilots, we can provision a small reserved pool for more realistic measures.
[04:18] Maya: About private deployments — if we can't allow egress at all, can Redwood ship an on-prem package?
[04:24] Jules: Yes, we have a private on-prem offering. It's heavier lift but supports full air-gapped deployment. Key integrations like KMS/HSM and audit log forwarding are supported.
[04:34] Ravi: How do you handle model version pinning and rollouts? We need reproducibility for customer incidents.
[04:39] Jules: You can pin model versions per route; rollouts support canary and A/B, plus automatic fallback to previous versions. All request logs include model version metadata.
[04:48] Maya: Any issues integrating with our observability stack — we use Datadog and Sentry?
[04:52] Samir: We export metrics via Prometheus scrape endpoints and have webhook/event integrations that can forward anomalies to Datadog or your incident system. Error traces can be exported to Sentry via custom hooks.
[05:03] Ravi: On quotas — do you support burst credits for traffic spikes? We expect big spikes around sales promotions.
[05:08] Jules: Dedicated pools include configurable burst capacity and autoscaling policies. For hosted, we can enable burst buffers for short windows but long sustained load should move to dedicated.
[05:19] Maya: Security checklist — do you have SOC2 and independent pen test reports we can review?
[05:24] Samir: Yes, SOC 2 Type II is available; we can share a redacted report and our security whitepaper.
[05:29] Elena: There's often small friction around SDK versions and model naming — you mentioned 'Redwood Serve' in docs — any plan to unify naming?
[05:35] Jules: We're in the process of renaming docs; you'll see legacy strings. The API surface is stable though — keys are the same.
[05:40] Speaker 1: (brief crosstalk)
[05:43] Maya: For our acceptance criteria: 95% p95 latency under 300ms for re-rank endpoint, 99.9% availability during peak, and predictable monthly cost within 10% — is that reasonable?
[05:56] Jules: Reasonable. For re-rank, quantify tokens per request and QPS; we'll map to latency curves and recommend dedicated sizing.
[06:07] Ravi: I'll send a 7-day token histogram and QPS by endpoint.
[06:10] Samir: Great — once you send that, Jules will propose a dedicated pilot config and we'll include cost estimates.
[06:18] Elena: On the LangChain example — can you show how to wire up our retriever to LlamaIndex and then call Redwood as the LLM?
[06:25] Jules: Yes, the sample repo shows LlamaIndex -> LangChain wrappers calling Redwood via SDK. It has env var examples for proxying through your server.
[06:33] Maya: Any concerns with data residency? We have EU customers and want data at rest in EU.
[06:38] Samir: We have region controls; for hosted you can pick EU region to keep data there. For dedicated and private you get more control over where logs and artifacts live.
[06:48] Ravi: About keys — KMS integration. Can Redwood connect to our AWS KMS or do you require keys in your vault?
[06:55] Jules: For hosted, we manage key rotation but can integrate with customer KMS for dedicated/private via AWS KMS or HSM. We'll detail modes in the security doc.
[07:06] Maya: Let's talk timeline — we want a POC within 2-3 weeks if possible.
[07:11] Samir: We can do a quick hosted POC in 1-2 weeks; dedicated pilot might take 2-4 weeks for provisioning.
[07:19] Elena: Pricing transparency — can you show sample per-token math for different batching/quantization settings?
[07:25] Samir: Yes, we'll send an example cost model spreadsheet showing options (onsite quantized variants lower token cost but might increase latency slightly).
[07:35] Ravi: Any known issues with LangChain streaming interrupt tokens? We've seen partial responses when network resets occur.
[07:42] Jules: We handle interrupted streams by providing resumable tokens in some cases and idempotency keys for replays. But network handling is partly on your proxy too.
[07:53] Maya: Great. Recap of next actions?
[07:56] Samir: I'll send pricing + hosted vs dedicated comparison + SOC2 redacted.
[08:01] Jules: I'll draft the benchmark plan, share LangChain/LlamaIndex examples, and a small load generator.
[08:07] Ravi: I'll send the traffic histogram and token estimates.
[08:10] Elena: We'll review and pick date for POC kickoff.
[08:13] Samir: Perfect, thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the SE kickoff.
[08:18] Maya: Thanks.

(End of call — total recorded ~52 minutes, some short audio gaps and minor transcription errors in proper nouns)
